stem: ______ is the functional group of carboxylic acid.
solution:
**(D)** \(-COOH\)

A carboxylic acid contains the carboxyl group \(-COOH\) as its functional group, for example ethanoic acid \(CH_3COOH\). The group \(-OH\) belongs to alcohols, \(-CHO\) to aldehydes and \(-NH_2\) to amines.

stem: The force acting on any object moving along a circle and directed towards the centre of the circle is called as ______.
solution:
**(C)** Centripetal force

For an object in uniform circular motion, the force that acts on it and is directed towards the centre of the circle is called the centripetal force ('centripetal' means centre seeking). Its magnitude is \(\dfrac{mv^2}{r}\).

stem: When electric current is passed through acidulated water ______ of water takes place.
solution:
**(C)** Electrolysis

When electric current is passed through acidulated water, water decomposes into hydrogen and oxygen gases: \(2H_2O_{(l)} \rightarrow 2H_{2(g)} + O_{2(g)}\). This decomposition takes place by means of electrical energy, so it is called electrolysis.

stem: In India the frequency of alternating current (AC) is ______.
solution:
**(B)** 50 Hz

The AC supplied in India changes its polarity 100 times every second, that is, it completes 50 cycles per second. Hence the frequency of AC in India is \(50\) Hz.

stem: The angle between the surface of a glass slab and incident ray is \(30^\circ\). The angle of incidence is ______.
solution:
**(B)** \(60^\circ\)

The angle of incidence is measured between the incident ray and the normal, and the normal is perpendicular (\(90^\circ\)) to the surface. \(\therefore\) angle of incidence \(= 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ\). Check: \(60^\circ + 30^\circ = 90^\circ\), the angle between the normal and the surface.

stem: Find odd one out: Voltmeter, Ammeter, Galvanometer, Thermometer.
solution: Odd one out: Thermometer. The voltmeter, ammeter and galvanometer are electrical measuring instruments (they measure potential difference, electric current and detect small currents), whereas a thermometer measures temperature.

subtopic: Free Fall and Acceleration due to Gravity
stem: State whether true or false: The weight of an object is constant everywhere.
solution: False. Weight is the force with which the earth attracts an object, \(W = mg\). The value of \(g\) changes from place to place (it is less at greater heights and at the equator than at the poles, and zero at the centre of the earth), so the weight of an object also changes from place to place. Only its mass stays constant.

stem: Complete the co-relation: Cooking of food : Chemical change :: Evaporation of water : ______.
solution: Physical change. When water evaporates only its state changes from liquid to vapour; no new substance is formed and the change is reversible, so it is a physical change.

stem: Give scientific reason: Stars appear to be higher in the sky as compared to its actual position.
solution: The density of air, and hence its refractive index, increases as the height above the earth's surface decreases. Light coming from a star therefore travels continuously from a rarer medium to a denser medium as it passes through the atmosphere, and keeps bending towards the normal. To an observer on the earth the light appears to come along the final direction of the bent ray, which points to a position higher than the real one. Hence stars appear to be higher in the sky as compared to their actual position.

stem: Give scientific reason: Elements belonging to the same group have the same valency.
solution: The valency of an element is determined by the number of electrons present in the outermost shell of its atoms (the valence electrons). All the elements in a group have the same number of valence electrons; for example lithium (2, 1), sodium (2, 8, 1) and potassium (2, 8, 8, 1) of group 1 each have one valence electron. Hence elements belonging to the same group have the same valency (all group 1 elements have valency 1).

stem: Give scientific reason: Geostationary satellites are not useful for studies of polar regions.
solution: Geostationary satellites revolve in an orbit at a height of about \(35780\) km that lies above the equator, and they take 24 hours for one revolution, so they remain above the same point on the equator. From this position they cannot properly observe the polar regions, which lie far from the equatorial plane. Hence geostationary satellites are not useful for studies of polar regions. For this purpose, elliptical medium earth orbits passing over the polar regions, called polar orbits, are used.

stem: The focal length of a convex lens is 40 cm. What is its power?
solution:
Given: focal length of the convex lens \(f = +40\) cm \(= +0.4\) m.

Power \(P = \dfrac{1}{f\ (\text{in m})} = \dfrac{1}{0.4\ \text{m}}\).

\(\therefore P = +2.5\) D (dioptre).

Check: \(\dfrac{1}{2.5\ \text{D}} = 0.4\) m \(= 40\) cm. The power is positive because a convex lens is a converging lens.

stem:
State the laws:
(a) Right hand thumb rule.
(b) Fleming's left hand rule.
solution:
(a) Right hand thumb rule: Imagine that the current-carrying conductor is held in the right hand so that the thumb points in the direction of the current. Then the direction in which the fingers curl around the conductor is the direction of the magnetic lines of force.
(b) Fleming's left hand rule: Stretch the thumb, index finger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the index finger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, then the thumb points in the direction of the force on the conductor.

stem: State Kepler's three laws.
solution:
Kepler's first law: The orbit of a planet is an ellipse with the Sun at one of the foci.

Kepler's second law: The line joining the planet and the Sun sweeps equal areas in equal intervals of time.

Kepler's third law: The square of the period of revolution of a planet around the Sun is directly proportional to the cube of the mean distance of the planet from the Sun. If \(T\) is the period of revolution and \(r\) the mean distance, then \(T^2 \propto r^3\), that is, \(\dfrac{T^2}{r^3} = K\), a constant.

stem:
An electric tungsten bulb is connected into a home circuit. The home electric supply runs at \(220\) V potential difference. When switch on, a current of \(0.45\) A flows through the bulb:
(a) What must be power (wattage) of the bulb?
(b) If it is kept on for \(10\) hours, how many units of electricity will be consumed?
solution:
Given: \(V = 220\) V, \(I = 0.45\) A, \(t = 10\) h.

(a) Power \(P = V \times I = 220\ \text{V} \times 0.45\ \text{A}\).
\(\therefore P = 99\) W. The wattage of the bulb is \(99\) W.

(b) Energy consumed \(= P \times t = 99\ \text{W} \times 10\ \text{h} = 990\ \text{Wh}\).
Since \(1\) unit \(= 1\ \text{kWh} = 1000\ \text{Wh}\),
\(\therefore\) energy consumed \(= \dfrac{990}{1000} = 0.99\) unit.

Check: a bulb of about \(100\) W used for \(10\) h uses about \(1\) kWh, which matches \(0.99\) unit.

stem: State the factors affecting the rate of chemical reaction. Explain any one of it.
solution:
Factors affecting the rate of a chemical reaction:

1. Nature of the reactants
2. Size of the particles of reactants
3. Concentration of the reactants
4. Temperature of the reaction
5. Catalyst

Explanation (size of the particles of reactants): Equal weights of pieces and of powder of Shahabad tile are taken in two test tubes and 10 ml of dilute HCl is added to each. The effervescence of \(CO_2\) is formed slowly with the pieces but at a faster speed with the powder. The powder offers a much larger surface for the acid to act on. Thus, smaller the size of the reactant particles, higher is the rate of the reaction.

subtopic: Latent Heat and Change of State
stem:
(a) What is meant by Regelation?
(b) What is the effect of pressure on melting point of ice?
(c) Write any one example of regelation.
solution:
(a) Regelation: The phenomenon in which ice converts to liquid due to applied pressure and then re-converts to ice once the pressure is removed is called regelation.
(b) The melting point of ice becomes lower than \(0\ ^\circ\)C when pressure is applied. So under pressure ice melts at \(0\ ^\circ\)C; when the pressure is removed the melting point is restored to \(0\ ^\circ\)C and the water freezes again.
(c) Example: An ice-ball is prepared by pressing shredded ice around the tip of a stick; the pressed ice melts slightly and refreezes into a solid ball when the pressure is released. (Similarly, a metal wire carrying weights passes through an ice slab without breaking it.)

stem:
Read the following passage and answer the questions given below:

**Space Debris and its management**

In addition to the artificial satellite, some other objects are also revolving around the earth. It includes, non-functional satellites, parts of the launcher detached during launching and debris generated due to collision of satellite with other satellite or any other object in the space. According to one estimation mode in 2016, there are about 2 crore pieces of length more than 1 cm, revolving around the earth! All this is nothing but the debris in space.

This debris can be harmful to the artificial satellites. It can collide with these satellites or spacecrafts and damage them. This debris is increasing day by day. Soon, it will be difficult to launch new spacecrafts. It is, therefore, very essential to manage the debris. Some studies and experiments are being done with this in view.

(a) What is meant by space debris?
(b) How it can be harmful to the artificial satellites?
(c) What efforts are being taken to manage it?
solution:
(a) Space debris means the objects, other than working artificial satellites, that keep revolving around the earth: non-functional satellites, parts of the launcher detached during launching, and debris generated by collisions of satellites with other satellites or other objects in space. In 2016 there were estimated to be about 2 crore such pieces longer than 1 cm.
(b) The debris can collide with artificial satellites or spacecraft and damage them. As the debris increases day by day, it will soon become difficult to launch new spacecraft safely.
(c) Since it is very essential to manage the debris, studies and experiments are being done to find ways of managing it, so that future satellites and spacecraft are no longer in danger.

stem: Observe the following diagrams and state the rules of refraction of light in different media using it.
solution:
Rules of refraction shown by the diagrams:

- Diagram (a): When a light ray passes from a rarer medium to a denser medium, it bends towards the normal, so the angle of refraction is smaller than the angle of incidence (\(r < i\)).
- Diagram (b): When a light ray passes from a denser medium to a rarer medium, it bends away from the normal, so the angle of refraction is greater than the angle of incidence (\(r > i\)).
- Diagram (c): When a light ray is incident normally (perpendicular) on the boundary between two media, it does not change its direction and hence is not refracted (\(i = r = 0^\circ\)).
figureNote: three ray diagrams labelled (a), (b), (c): (a) ray from rarer medium into denser medium bending towards the normal (angles i, r); (b) ray from denser medium into rarer medium bending away from the normal (angles i, r); (c) ray incident normally from rarer into denser medium passing undeviated; p-02 (Page 3/4)

subtopic: Early Attempts and Mendeleev's Periodic Table
stem: Write demerits of Mendeleev's periodic table.
solution:
Demerits of Mendeleev's periodic table:

1. The whole number atomic masses of cobalt (Co) and nickel (Ni) are the same, so there was an ambiguity regarding their sequence in the table.
2. Isotopes were discovered long after the table was put forth. As isotopes have the same chemical properties but different atomic masses, placing them in the table posed a challenge.
3. When elements are arranged in increasing order of atomic masses, the rise in atomic mass is not uniform, so it was not possible to predict how many elements could be discovered between two heavy elements.
4. Position of hydrogen: hydrogen shows similarity with the halogens (molecular formula \(H_2\), like \(F_2\) and \(Cl_2\)) as well as with the alkali metals (compounds \(HCl\), \(H_2O\), \(H_2S\) like \(NaCl\), \(Na_2O\), \(Na_2S\)), so its correct position could not be decided.

(b) For what purpose the above method is used?
(c) Write two properties which are used in the method.
(d) What is the use of agitator?

solution:
(a) The method shown is the froth floatation method.
(b) It is used for the concentration of ores, that is, separating the gangue from certain sulphide ores so that the proportion of the metal compound increases.
(c) It is based on two opposite properties of the particles: hydrophobic (the metal sulphide particles get wetted mainly with oil) and hydrophilic (the gangue particles get wetted with water).
(d) The agitator rotates around its axis in the centre of the floatation tank and stirs the mixture. Due to this agitation, oil (such as pine oil), water and the air bubbles from the blown air together form a foam (froth), which rises to the surface carrying the ore particles.
(e) Zinc blende (\(ZnS\)) is concentrated by this method (copper pyrite, \(CuFeS_2\), is another such ore).

subtopic: Human Eye and Defects of Vision
stem:
Observe the following figure and answer the questions given below:
(a) Name the defect of vision represented in the above figure.
(b) State the reasons for this defect.
(c) How is it corrected?
(d) Draw the diagram to show the correction of this defect.
solution:
(a) The figure shows rays from a nearby object being focused behind the retina. The defect is farsightedness (hypermetropia): the eye sees distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects distinctly, because its near point shifts farther than 25 cm.
(b) Reasons for hypermetropia:
1. The curvature of the cornea and the eye lens decreases, so the converging power of the lens becomes less.
2. The eyeball becomes flattened, so the distance between the lens and the retina decreases.
(c) It is corrected by using a convex lens of proper focal length. The convex lens converges the incident rays before they reach the eye lens, and the eye lens then converges them further to form the image on the retina.
(d) Diagram (to be drawn by the candidate): a hypermetropic eye with a convex lens placed in front of it. Rays from a nearby object (at the normal near point, 25 cm) pass through the convex lens, are made to converge a little, and after refraction by the eye lens meet exactly on the retina. Labels: nearby object, convex lens, hypermetropic eye, eye lens, retina, image on retina.
figureNote: ray diagram of an eye: rays from a near point object on the axis enter the eye and converge to a point behind the retina (hypermetropic eye); p-03 (Page 4/4)
